analysis.title: GS Shelofsky - IG Credit Week in Review 22 Nov 2026
key_insights: IG100 closed 10bps wider on the week, tied for the worst week of the year, wider on all 5 sessions, with average daily move 2x the YTD average.
Street was net lifted on 1.3bn of risk Friday and ETFs traded 0-1bp cheap to NAV, which the author reads as credit not being caught wrong-way.
Willingness to step into risk, especially in storied beta names, is near multi-year lows, producing outsized moves on modest selling amid poor seasonal liquidity.

IG cash (Bberg index) closed +10bps wider vs +6bps implied by equity beta, while CDXIG was +6bps vs +8.6bps implied, suggesting cash move was exaggerated by liquidity and credit investors are broadly onsides.
Debt/equity correlation bottomed mid-summer during the AI capex funding trade, which hit hyperscaler credit. This week's widening was broad-based and far more correlated.
Hyperscaler basket traded at 2x beta vs IG100 over the last month vs 1.5x average, with correlation at highs of 0.93 vs 0.74, so it reflects macro de-risking rather than selling on the capex story.
Goldman and Apollo led a 44bn financing across tranches for SpaceX's GPU purchase. The public tranche was a 25bn A- rated 3.6WAL 6.5y bond priced at +345bps over the 3y, pricing north of 8.25%.
The SpaceX GPU deal closed 15bps tight to pricing and up nearly 1pt including the rate rally despite Friday's sell-off. Chip financing is flagged as a top focus for 2027.
3-7y was the most net sold part of the IG curve WTD at 1.7bn, and curves in AI and beta names are at or near YTD flats due to heavy supply.
HY spreads closed 51bps wider, the worst week of the year, and 45% of HY still trades tight to 200bps. Up to 300bn of chip financing supply next year could crowd out generic HY demand.
GS Vol Panic Indicator at 9.8/10, with record de-risking and de-grossing, third straight week of global equity selling, and ETF shorts up 11%, the largest weekly move in 5 years.
Near-term view: tactically bullish IG cash after the move to the wides, but rallies are still to be sold. Selling vol is seen as more attractive than cash for real upside exposure.
